concurrency_note: check_single_writer is a single-pass static scan of checked-in source at a fixed SHA — there is no concurrent/racing writer dimension in the artifact itself to evade (the invariant it checks, an atomic single write PATH in code, is a design-time property, not a runtime race).

authority_boundary.proves: every writer of a single-write-path invariant's controls_field, found by scanning a Go/Mongo/SQL source tree for assignments, struct-literal sets, bson $set mutations, and SQL UPDATE ... SET, is reported as a violation unless its enclosing symbol or file is in sanctioned_writers; and — as of #282 — that every file in the scanned population was actually READ: a file the scanner could not decode or open is named in `unscanned` rather than silently dropped, so a zero finding count is no longer ambiguous between 'nothing wrong' and 'nothing read'
authority_boundary.artifact: a git worktree copy of the target repo's tracked source tree (vendor/node_modules/dist/build/.git excluded by design)
assumptions: the invariant carries well-formed controls_field + sanctioned_writers metadata (structured state-machines.json or prose @cw-writes tag)
a writer that never appears as a literal quoted/assigned field-name token (fully dynamic field construction through reflection or string concatenation) is not detectable by a regex scanner
vendor/node_modules/dist/build subtrees are explicitly out of scope (SKIP_PARTS) — a writer placed there will not be found
test-file writes are treated as fixtures, never violations, per the is_test heuristic

a mildly-corrupt file is scanned LOSSILY rather than skipped (utf-8 errors='replace'): a replacement character cannot fabricate a write site or an annotation, so a lossy read can yield a false negative but never a false positive

what this does NOT prove: that a lossily-decoded file was fully understood — only that it was not silently dropped. A file decoding to >30% replacement characters is reported unscanned instead of scanned-as-garbage
BOM-less UTF-16 is detected by NUL-byte interleaving density, not by a BOM or a replacement-character ratio — the ratio for that case is 0%, which is precisely why it went undetected in the first cut

seeded_defect_trials.injected: internal/admin/handlers.go: ChangePlan writes provider.plan via bson $set, outside INV-bil-001's sanctioned_writers
internal/db/leak.go: an unsanctioned write of provider.active_owner_count hidden inside a nested anonymous closure with no directly-enclosing named function at the write site
internal/wrappers/generic.go: a generically-named SetField helper writes provider.stripe_plan via bson $set — indirection through a wrapper function, not the sanctioned symbol name
vendor/thirdparty/patch.go: an unsanctioned write of provider.stripe_plan placed inside the vendor/ subtree, which SKIP_PARTS excludes by design

validated_by: chief-wiggum#168 (re-validated post #181/#182 scanner changes); re-authored for chief-wiggum#213 Phase D: the module gained the --scope domain-authority split (repo-wide detection, in-domain vs boundary finding classification; boundary findings never affect the exit code) and the explicit applicability verdict (inapplicable when no single-write-path invariants are defined — Phase E), and artifacts.py (whose scope-matching rule decides the classification) joined the scanner-version hash inputs; without --scope the writer/violation semantics are unchanged and all trials re-verified live by tests/test_gate_validation_retroactive.py; re-authored for the #215 /adopt review fixes: the gate now honors adoption grandfathers — <meta root>/adoption/grandfathered.json (resolver default, --grandfather PATH override); an in-domain violation matching a NON-EXPIRED check_single_writer:<INV-id>:<field>:<file> entry moves to the 'grandfathered' section (reported, non-blocking under --gate coverage) and an EXPIRED entry blocks again labeled 'EXPIRED grandfather'; chief_wiggum/grandfather.py (the shared waiver reader) joined the scanner-version hash inputs; all other finding classes and exit semantics unchanged and all trials re-verified live by tests/test_gate_validation_retroactive.py; re-authored for chief-wiggum#259 (C#/.NET): config/languages.json joined chief_wiggum/languages.py as a scanner_version hash input. Moving an extension between `generic_tier` and `unsupported_extensions` — which is exactly what #259 does for `.cs` — changes which files this scanner walks with no code change at all, so before this the record could stay `passing` straight through a real coverage change (the CTR-fh-041 silent-staleness class, one layer out in the data instead of the code). Verified by mutating the extension set and observing the version move. No new finding class, and no change to thresholds, exit codes or report shape; all trials and clean-corpus runs re-verified live; further re-authored after the #259 review: chief_wiggum/write_emission.py gained a C# method/property regex (CS_FUNC_RE) so `.cs` write sites resolve an enclosing symbol — without one, a symbol-sanctioned writer could not be distinguished from an unsanctioned one in C#; `.cs` line comments are now stripped too, so a field named in a `//` comment is not read as a write. `.cs` was previously unscanned entirely, so no existing target's findings change; re-authored for chief-wiggum#282: the bulk source scan now reads through the shared chief_wiggum/textio.py decode boundary (a new finding-affecting scanner_version hash input) instead of a bare path.read_text(). Before this, a single non-UTF-8 file anywhere in the scanned population raised UnicodeDecodeError and the gate produced NO VERDICT AT ALL — the pre-existing `except OSError` guards never caught it, since UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError. Files that cannot be read are now reported as `unscanned` WITH their paths. That list is REPORT-ONLY: it is excluded from soundness_ok/coverage_ok and cannot by itself flip the gate under --gate, so no new blocking finding class and no change to exit semantics — as with the #278 re-author, the seeded trials and clean-corpus run are unchanged and were re-verified live by tests/test_gate_validation_retroactive.py. Orchestrator validation additionally caught a defect in the first cut of the fix: a BOM-less UTF-16 file decoded 'successfully' as UTF-8 with ZERO replacement characters (ASCII-in-UTF-16 is s\x00t\x00r\x00..., and NUL is valid UTF-8), yielding text no scan regex could match — the file was reported clean having never been read. That is fixed by NUL-interleaving detection ahead of the UTF-8 attempt; see #289.; re-authored for chief-wiggum#295: chief_wiggum/hashing.py gained ID_BEARING_ARTIFACTS/find_id_bearing_artifacts/scan_malformed_ids (reusing trace_ids.near_miss_ids from #281 rather than a second detector). hashing.py is a finding-affecting scanner_version hash input for every shipped gate, so this gate's version moved even though its OWN behaviour is unchanged — trials and clean-corpus runs are unchanged and were re-verified live.
